question: Do we have a tomato line that is drought tolerant and powdery mildew resistant, and is it ready for spring planting?

nodes.label: A-INQ-001
nodes.description: Customer inquiry: drought tolerance + powdery mildew resistance for tomato, spring planting in Texas Zone 8

nodes.label: A-TRT-PMR
nodes.description: Powdery mildew resistance trait ontology entry

nodes.label: A-GEN-DRT2
nodes.description: Drought response marker 2, linked to A-TRT-DRT, confidence 0.91

nodes.label: A-GEN-PMR3
nodes.description: Powdery mildew resistance marker 3, linked to A-TRT-PMR, confidence 0.88

nodes.label: A-CUL-TOM-014
nodes.description: Solara-14: best candidate with both DRT2 and PMR3 markers, status field_ready

nodes.label: A-CUL-TOM-022
nodes.description: DryShield-22: has both markers but field validation incomplete, status greenhouse_validated

nodes.label: A-CUL-TOM-031
nodes.description: Arida-31: drought only, lacks PMR3 marker, status field_ready

nodes.label: A-TRL-GH-001/002
nodes.description: Drought drydown assay results for A-CUL-TOM-014: pass, wilting scores 1.4-1.6

nodes.label: A-TRL-GH-003/004

nodes.label: A-TRL-FD-002
nodes.description: Field trial in A-FLD-BLOCK-3 (Texas Zone 8, 2025-Fall): pass, yield 42.6 kg/plot, disease 1.1

nodes.label: A-FLD-BLOCK-3
nodes.description: Texas Zone 8, sandy loam, ready, 1,200 m², planting window 2026-04-20 to 2026-05-18

nodes.label: SOIL-RPT-2026-033

nodes.label: Answer: Solara-14 Ready
